Fit a Topics over Time model

Source: R/tot.R
tot.Rd

Fits the Topics over Time (TOT) model of Wang and McCallum (2006) by collapsed Gibbs sampling. Each topic has a multinomial distribution over words and a Beta distribution over (normalized) time, so topics are shaped jointly by word co-occurrence and by when documents were written.

Usage

tot(
  x,
  time,
  k,
  alpha = 50/k,
  beta = 0.1,
  n_iter = 500L,
  time_weight = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A document-term matrix of counts with documents in rows: a base matrix, a Matrix sparse matrix, a quanteda dfm, or a tm DocumentTermMatrix.

time

Document timestamps, one per row of x: numeric, Date or POSIXct.

k

Number of topics.

alpha

Symmetric Dirichlet prior on document-topic proportions. Default 50 / k, as in the paper.

beta

Symmetric Dirichlet prior on topic-word distributions.

n_iter

Number of Gibbs sweeps.

time_weight

Exponent on the time likelihood, balancing time against words. A number (1 gives the sampler exactly as in the paper), or "inverse_length" for 1 / N_d, the alternative the paper describes, which treats each document's timestamp as one observation. The paper reports that results are sensitive to this setting.

verbose

Print progress every 50 iterations.

Value

An object of class "tot", a list with

phi

k x vocabulary matrix of topic-word probabilities.

theta

documents x k matrix of document-topic proportions.

psi

k x 2 matrix of Beta shape parameters on the normalized time scale.

topic_size

Number of tokens assigned to each topic.

plus the settings used and the information needed to map times back to the original scale.

Details

Timestamps are mapped linearly onto the open interval (0, 1) using the range of time. The Beta parameters are re-estimated by the method of moments after every sweep, as in the paper, with both shapes kept at or above 1 (same mean, higher concentration) so densities stay bounded and topics cannot lock onto the earliest or latest documents.

References

Wang, X. and McCallum, A. (2006). Topics over time: a non-Markov continuous-time model of topical trends. Proceedings of the 12th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 424–433. doi:10.1145/1150402.1150450

See also

predict.tot(), topic_time(), terms.tot(), plot.tot()

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_tot(n_docs = 100, n_topics = 3)
fit <- tot(sim$x, sim$time, k = 3, n_iter = 50)
fit
#> Topics over Time model
#>   topics: 3, documents: 100, vocabulary: 100
#>   iterations: 50, alpha: 16.66667, beta: 0.1, time_weight: 1
#>   time range: 0.0355636 to 0.9930231
terms(fit, 5)
#>      Topic1 Topic2 Topic3
#> [1,] "w100" "w6"   "w6"  
#> [2,] "w26"  "w26"  "w75" 
#> [3,] "w12"  "w97"  "w30" 
#> [4,] "w87"  "w33"  "w26" 
#> [5,] "w84"  "w51"  "w86"
